annotations.text:
A · TERMINAL

Monospace-forward, hairlines only, not one card or rounded box anywhere. Dense and precise, closest to the Codex app you showed me.

Accent is a single vermilion used almost nowhere, so where it appears it means something.

Against it: this is the direction most likely to read as a developer tool rather than something you learn in.

B · PRESS

The question is set like a printed page. Serif at 34px, a wide measure, warm near-black, and rules instead of boxes. The layout is asymmetric on purpose.

Accent is a printing red.

Against it: serif at that size eats room, and the density you want in a graph or a code editor fights this.

C · INSTRUMENT

The glassy one. A blurred, saturated sidebar over a lit ground, fine grain over everything, soft panels with a one-pixel top highlight.

This one also shows the component idea: a real code editor with language tabs, sent to your agent for review against the actual file.

Against it: glass costs performance in a webview, and it is the direction closest to what everyone else is shipping.

Same question, same content, three visual languages. Pick one and I will rebuild all six screens in it.

You can also take parts: A's density with C's glass, or B's typography on A's chrome. Say which and I will make that the fourth.
